description: Framework screen output. One file per framework at data/screens/<framework>.json. Written by .claude/commands/<framework>.md via scripts/apply-screen.mjs. Consumed by /screens. Each `screens[]` entry is one company's rubric-score card — five dimensions per framework, composite = mean of dimension scores. Two frameworks live today: blue-ocean (Kim/Mauborgne value-innovation rubric) and rule-breaker (Motley Fool top-dog / first-mover rubric). Schema is framework-agnostic.

framework.description: Which rubric this file scores against.

generatedAt.description: Last time apply-screen.mjs updated the file (individual per-ticker entries carry their own screenedAt below).

dimensions.description: The rubric dimensions in canonical order. Each screens[].dimensions[] entry MUST have an entry per key here. Frozen once a framework version ships.

key.description: Short slug used as JSON key in per-ticker dimension arrays (e.g. 'value-innovation').

label.description: Human-readable dimension name shown in the UI.

description.description: Rubric text — how to interpret a high vs low score on this dimension. Shown in tooltip.

screens.description: Per-ticker screen cards. Append-only within a framework — apply-screen.mjs merges by ticker (later screening overwrites the ticker's card).

compositeScore.description: Mean of the dimension scores. Rounded to 1 decimal.

dimensions.description: One entry per rubric dimension (matches the file-level dimensions[] order + count).

score.description: 0-100. 0 = strong negative fit, 50 = neutral, 100 = perfect fit.

rationale.description: One line explaining the score. Cite a fact — no speculation.

verdict.description: One-sentence overall read on the company against this framework. Neutral tone — no target price, no directional trade call.
